ops.title: git resolves a short remote-tracking name through refs/heads first — verify one ref, compare another
ops.body:
Reproduced 2026-08-01 against git 2.55.0 while adjudicating a review finding on internal/cli/restack.go gtRestackTrunkRef.

A short name like `origin/main` is NOT a safe stand-in for `refs/remotes/origin/main`. Per gitrevisions(7), git checks `refs/heads/<name>` BEFORE `refs/remotes/<name>`, so a local branch literally named `origin/main` shadows the remote-tracking ref:

```
git update-ref refs/remotes/origin/main $SHA_A   # verified by show-ref --verify --quiet → exit 0
git update-ref refs/heads/origin/main   $SHA_B   # decoy

git rev-parse origin/main
  warning: refname origin/main is ambiguous.
  <SHA_B>                                        # NOT the ref that was verified

git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main feature              → exit 1   WRONG
git merge-base --is-ancestor refs/remotes/origin/main feature → exit 0   correct
```

The trap has a specific shape worth remembering: code that probes with the FULLY QUALIFIED ref (`show-ref --verify refs/remotes/<r>/<t>`) and then RETURNS the short form has already proven it knows which ref is trustworthy, and throws that precision away. Verify one ref, compare another.

Compounding it: `gitIsAncestor` (internal/cli/ship.go) treats `merge-base --is-ancestor` exit 1 as a clean "not an ancestor" and does not inspect stderr, so gits `warning: refname ... is ambiguous` is swallowed and the wrong verdict is indistinguishable from an ordinary one.

Rule for ccx: any ref fed to a git plumbing comparison is fully qualified. Short forms are for user-facing labels only.
